sources.entry: Ampache - Web based audio/video streaming application. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: Ampache is a web-based audio and video streaming application and file manager for accessing a personal music and video library from most internet-connected devices.
summary.what_it_does: Ampache is a PHP web application that streams audio and video from a user's own file collection through a browser or client apps. It builds its library from metadata embedded in files and from file names, and presents an already organized collection rather than organizing files itself. The README describes a documented Ampache API, and the develop branch (Ampache 8) adds an opt-in Jellyfin-compatible API that lets third-party Jellyfin clients such as Finamp, Symfonium and gelly browse and stream the library. Requirements are listed per release line, with a web server (Apache is the most tested; lighttpd, nginx and IIS are also mentioned), MySQL or MariaDB, and a set of PHP extensions. Optional modules enable LDAP authentication, UPnP and a Yourls plugin.
use_cases: stream personal music library from any device
serve video files over the web
how_to_run: Install a supported web server, PHP (version depends on release line) and MySQL/MariaDB
Clone or extract the Ampache release into your web root
Follow the installation guide in the Ampache wiki
Review the basic configuration guide after installation
Upgrading: move the old directory aside, extract the new copy, then copy back config/ampache.cfg.php and any rest/.htaccess or play/.htaccess files
notable: Jellyfin-compatible API (opt-in) for third-party Jellyfin clients
Reads metadata from embedded tags and file names rather than managing files
Supports both audio and video streaming
caveats: Ampache 8 (develop branch) is a work in progress, may be unstable, and requires PHP 8.5+
The recommended stable line is release7; PHP and Node.js version requirements vary by release
Relies on correctly tagged files; it is not a media organizer
